blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Finance (DOF) has signed the $1.5-billion financing extended by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to help fund the government’s measures to cushion the impact of the Middle East crisis. The parties signed the agreement, named the Assistance for Greater Resilience and Alleviation of Poverty (Agapay), on Oct. 6. READ: DOF to tap up to $1.5B in ADB support for oil shock response The financing, equivalent to roughly P90.8 billion, will provide budgetary support for the government’s Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (Uplift). “Agapay will help the government sustain its response to the economic […]...
